adds.title: A closed task's temp folders are queued at its close, not 24 h later
adds.why: (@nha, 2026-11-11: « if tackled first instead of the many one offs we would not be talking about this ») 12 GB of merged tasks' scratch builds waited out temps.rs's 24 h idle while the disk was red (2026-11-12).
adds.done_when: 1. dash land and a run's close queue the closed task's session folders under Claude's temp root at once; test temps_of_a_closed_task_queue_at_close. 2. A folder whose session still runs is never queued, closed task or not; test a_live_session_folder_stays_at_close. 3. After merge: no folder under /private/tmp/claude-501 belongs to a task closed over 2 hours ago (ls against dash task state).

adds.title: rust/ui-spike retired: what dash still uses moves into the workspace
adds.why: (@nha, 2026-11-11: « if tackled first instead of the many one offs we would not be talking about this ») No job compiles ui-spike: its dioxus-page broke on main and its Cargo.lock went stale unseen (rust-hooks-rest-port, 2026-11-12).
adds.done_when: 1. dash's theme freshness test and anything else dash reads from rust/ui-spike live in a workspace crate; test names listed in the PR. 2. rust/ui-spike is deleted, its ci-mirror.txt line and workspace_rules' lockfile entry with it; cargo nextest run -p dash-gate passes. 3. After merge: git ls-files rust/ui-spike prints nothing on main and the mirror is green.

adds.title: dash review next hands out PRs from Rust; the review lane never waits on Elixir
adds.why: (@nha, 2026-11-10: « remember we move to rust. no more elixir, so if something needs fixing port and then fix ») The review lane waited over an hour on 2026-11-12 for the Elixir app's review next while PRs 1460, 1480, 1484 and 1485 sat green.
adds.done_when: 1. dash review next (Rust) picks the oldest green PR no run, reviewer or hold claims and records the claim; a test with a stand-in forge. 2. A PR held by its own run or by dash pr hold is never handed out; a test each. 3. It answers within 2 s while a whole-store write runs; a test at that limit. 4. After merge: the review lane's pane runs the Rust command and reviews a PR the same hour one turns green.

board.title: dash task show <reviewer id> prints its live session, not « no task »
board.why: (@nha, 2026-11-02: « waste of time and waste of tokens ») review-app-emfile (10-31) and review-lane (11-04) read « no task » and doubted their report would land.
board.done_when: 1. dash task show review-<x> prints the reviewer's PR, pane, last start and last report from task events when no tasks.edn row exists; a test 2. A test on a task with a merged :pr and a later PR on its branch: the reviewer row's :pr and done-when name the later PR.

board.why: (@nha, 2026-11-11: « the discard/send should be closer to the previous elixir app (Send in blue, and trash icon). Send should be blue imo. red = danger, green = safety, but sending is neither. ») One fix in the Composer reaches every compose box.

The text form still reads Discard and Send, and the surface crate's tests pass 3. theme.css: --color-primary is blue in the light and dark themes, --color-success stays green 4. /design, card 'With its actions': 'Do it' shows blue 5. the slint mirror in rust/ui-spike/slint-design uses the same blue

board.title: Taking a to_process request is a dash command; agent_inbox.py goes
board.why: (@nha, 2026-11-10: « all these python scripts are also very brittle. we want to move all logic to rust and have it well tested. ») rust-hooks-rest-port kept agent_inbox.py: Dashboard.Watch's request card still names it.

The request card Rust's watcher writes names dash inbox take; Dashboard.Watch's card named retired with the Elixir watcher off. 3. agent_inbox.py deleted; the session-start hook calls dash; scripts count lowered.

board.title: One Rust gate on every outgoing message; dash mail send in Rust; the .py goes
board.why: (@nha, 2026-11-10: « all these python scripts are also very brittle. we want to move all logic to rust and have it well tested. ») rust-hooks-rest-port kept outbound_gate.py: Dashboard.Webmail's send still calls it.
board.done_when: 1. One Rust gate (banned phrases with scopes, Jev's reads-as-AI and length verdicts on the exact text) every send path calls; a test per path. 2. dash mail send <id> is Rust and calls it; each send logged as outbound.jsonl's lines are; a test. 3. LinkedIn sends (send_message, reply_in_thread, message_job_poster, connect notes) pass it through dash hook; a test each. 4. Dashboard.Webmail's send named retired; outbound_gate.py and its drafts.check call deleted; scripts count lowered. 5. After merge: one approved draft sent with dash mail send from Rust, its log line read back.

board.title: dash ci rerun refuses a head the orchestrator holds, and ci why says so
board.why: (@nha, 2026-10-29: « You fixed the mistake but didn't find the cause and what could actually fix that class of errors right ? ») The review lane reran 4 held runs: ci why said re-run, and the hold was only a comment.
board.done_when: 1. A hold names its reason and the PR it waits on in one row a command reads: a test sets and lifts it. 2. dash ci rerun refuses a run under a hold, naming both: a test per case, held and not. 3. dash ci why prints the hold in place of its re-run advice: a test per case. 4. dash review next claims no PR under a hold: a test per case.

board.title: A helper reviewing a PR claims it first, so no second reviewer starts
board.why: (@nha, 2026-10-22: « No double work. ») 2026-10-29: the orchestrator's helper reviewed PR 635 with no dash review claim, and the PM pass started its own reviewer on it.
board.done_when: 1. An Agent call whose prompt reviews a PR number with no live claim is refused, naming dash review claim: the hook's test. 2. A PrLane test: a PR whose handover went red while the app resumes its reviewer is not claimed by dash review next.

board.title: The PR lane leaves hand-backs to the PM's reviewers, inside 40 turns
board.why:
(@nha, 2026-10-30: « Things slowing us down should be picked as priority items. »)
review-lane passed its 40 turns tonight: each hand-back and each new PR restarts its loop.
board.done_when: 1. A hand-back on a PR the lane handed over resumes a PM reviewer, never the lane: a test.

board.title: dash review handover takes over the review lane's own claim
board.why: handover.ex:85 refuses 'review-lane holds a claim on 894' though the lane holds it; it took a release first. (@nha, 2026-10-25: « one sessoin continuously reviewing/simplifying/merging »)

Claim holder --push names the session that handed over (the record's by) too: a merge_claim selftest case passes review-lane's push. 3. Any other session's push to that branch is still refused, in the same selftest.

board.title: A done task's reviewer starts once its pane is gone, without the orchestrator

board.title: The orchestrator's gh pr merge passes a PR the review lane holds

board.title: A pane's failure seen by its state within a minute; every wake has an outcome
board.why: (@nha, 2026-11-02: « I asked for such a status check a bunch of times fyi, we need to reliably detect failures / stuck panes automatically and alert the orchestrator ») stuck-pane-watch waits 5 h of silence; 9 vibe panes printed their failure at once and sat 3 h.
board.done_when: 1. Dashboard.Watch matches a pane's last lines to a signature list (env: No such file, limit dialog, Error 143, bare prompt) and wakes within a minute 2. The list is data, grown per incident; every wake records its outcome, and one with none after 15 minutes is a dash asks entry 3. Tests on a stand-in herdr: a failing pane wakes once in a minute; a wake with no outcome escalates 4. A test: a screen with a done line above a running tool call is read as working, not done 5. A test: release of a claim whose pane shows a running tool call is refused naming the pane
